fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. Paul, the apostle writing this letter, says, “…I will go on to visions and revelations from the Lord.” (2 Corinthians 12:1) He just said there's nothing to gain, and he keeps going anyway. So the next part is all about what the Lord showed him.

This one is False, friend. Paul says, “The things he heard were inexpressible, things that man is not permitted to tell.” (2 Corinthians 12:4) So the man was not free to share them. He heard them, but telling them was not permitted.

This one is True, baker. Paul says, “…I will not boast about myself, except in my weaknesses.” (2 Corinthians 12:5) So about himself, weaknesses are the only thing he'll boast in. Most of us would list our best moments, and Paul hands over his weaknesses instead.

Weakness, baker. The Lord says, “…My power is perfected in weakness.” (2 Corinthians 12:9) That's strange to our ears, because we expect power to show up where things are strong. But He says it plain, and Paul takes Him at His word.

That's it. Paul says, “Therefore I will boast all the more gladly in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest on me.” (2 Corinthians 12:9) Notice the word gladly. That comes right after the Lord says, “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.”

Strong, baker! Paul writes, “For when I am weak, then I am strong.” (2 Corinthians 12:10) It sounds like a riddle. Right before it, the Lord says His power is perfected in weakness (2 Corinthians 12:9), and Paul says he'll boast so that the power of Christ may rest on him.

Alone is a heavy word, and I know that feeling. But it's not the word Paul writes. He says, “For when I am weak, then I am strong.” (2 Corinthians 12:10) And right before that, the Lord tells him, “My grace is sufficient for you…” (2 Corinthians 12:9)
